answer: The cheapest real defence: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because summit only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, lotus is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any ocean approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
